activeLock.owner: The instance owner is always active.
activeLock.agent: An agent's account follows its agent.
activeLock.scim: Your identity provider (SCIM) decides which accounts are active.

users.deactivateBody: They are signed out at once and cannot sign in or use their API keys until you turn the account back on. Their MCP connections and the invites they sent are removed. Nothing else is deleted.

userPanel.unconfirmedHint: Confirm it here when the link never reached them.
userPanel.noAccessHint: This account reaches nothing until someone invites it to a project.
userPanel.deleteHint: Issues and comments stay, with the author unassigned.
userPanel.deleteConfirmWithProjects: {count, plural, one {Delete account and project} other {Delete account and projects}}
userPanel.deleteMessage: {name} loses access to this instance. Issues and comments they wrote stay, with the author unassigned. This cannot be undone.
userPanel.deleteWorkspaceNote: A workspace this account owns is deleted with it while it has no projects or AI agents. Otherwise it passes to you, with everything the account owned alone in it.
userPanel.soleOwnerTitle: {count, plural, one {Only owner of a project} other {Only owner of # projects}}
userPanel.soleOwnerHint: {count, plural, one {Once the account is gone, nobody can manage it.} other {Once the account is gone, nobody can manage them.}}
userPanel.deleteWithProjects: {count, plural, one {Delete the project with the account} other {Delete the projects with the account}}
userPanel.deleteWithProjectsOff: Or cancel and add a second owner first.

projectPanel.noMembersHint: Nobody can reach this project until someone is invited to it.

teamPanel.noProjectsHint: This team owns no projects yet.
teamPanel.noMembersHint: Nobody belongs to this team yet.

roles.defaultUndeletable: The default role cannot be deleted

general.mcpEnabledHint: A new project starts open to MCP clients when its team has MCP on. Existing projects keep their setting.
general.personalWorkspacesHint: Each person gets a workspace of their own, named after them. Off, new accounts get none, and people work only in workspaces they are added to. Existing workspaces stay.
general.inviteSearchHint: Team owners and managers can find accounts from every workspace by name or email. Matches appear as they type in the invite dialog. Off, they enter the full address.
general.sharingEnabledHint: Off, existing links stop opening until this is on again, and nobody can share. On, each workspace decides whether its documents, issues and views can be shared by link.
general.apiDocsAudienceHint: In the app and at the API's /docs address.
general.keyRequestsPerMinuteHint: How many requests one key can send per minute, MCP tool calls included. Each API replica counts on its own. 0 sets no limit.
general.keyRequestsPerMinuteInvalid: Enter a whole number from 0 to {max}.
general.embedSitesHint: Only these sites can embed documents, issues and views shared by public link. With none listed, no site can. Enter each as https://example.com, separated by commas.
general.embedSitesInvalid: Enter each site as https://example.com, without a path.
general.embedSaved: Trusted sites saved. They apply within a minute.
general.traceRetentionHint: A trace records the model and tool calls of one agent run. After this time it is deleted, and usage dashboards stop counting the run.
general.maxRunTimeHint: A run that takes longer is stopped and saved as failed. An agent's own limit can only be shorter. Chats have no limit.
general.concurrentRunsHint: How many agent runs work at once on this instance. The rest wait in the queue. Chats and external agents don't count. 0 sets no limit.
general.concurrentRunsInvalid: Enter a whole number from 0 to {max}.
general.answerLimitHint: How many characters of an agent's answer are saved. The rest is cut off. Chats show the whole answer, but external agents get back only the saved part as history. 0 sets no limit.
general.answerLimitInvalid: Enter a whole number from 0 to {max, number}.
general.answerLimitNone: No limit. Long answers are saved whole and can make agent run lists slow to load.

authentication.registrationHint: Who can create an account and how long invites stay valid.
authentication.registrationPasswordlessNote: People sign up and reset passwords through the sign-in provider.
authentication.inviteTtlDaysHint: An invite stops working this many days after it is created. A new value also applies to existing invites. 0 means invites never expire.
authentication.inviteTtlDaysInvalid: Enter a whole number of days from 0 to {max}.
authentication.allowedEmailDomainsHint: Only addresses at these domains can create an account, including through an invite. Existing accounts keep their access. Separate domains with commas. A subdomain needs its own entry. Leave empty to allow any address.
authentication.allowedEmailDomainsInvalid: Enter domains like example.com, up to 100.

open.label: Open
open.description: Anyone can create an account on the sign-up page.
open.descriptionPasswordless: Anyone who signs in with the provider for the first time gets an account.

invite.label: Invite only
invite.description: Only addresses with a pending invite can create an account.
invite.descriptionPasswordless: Signing in with the provider creates an account only for an address with a pending invite.

closed.label: Closed
closed.description: Nobody can create an account. Existing accounts keep signing in.
closed.descriptionPasswordless: Signing in with the provider creates no account. Existing accounts keep signing in.

authentication.needsProvider: First set up an email provider in Integrations → Email provider.
authentication.requireVerificationHint: People must confirm their email address before signing in with a password. This includes existing accounts: the sign-in form offers to resend the confirmation link.
authentication.magicLinkHint: People can sign in with a link sent to their email. It works only while Email and password is on.
authentication.trustProviderEmailsHint: Google and OpenID Connect sign people in to the account with the same email address, even if nobody confirmed it. Turn this on only if you control who registers at the provider, or someone could take over an account.
authentication.emailPasswordHint: People sign up and sign in with an email and a password. When off, they sign in only through a sign-in provider or a passkey.
authentication.needsSso: First set up a sign-in provider in Integrations → Auth provider.
authentication.signInLimitsHint: How many requests one IP address can send to each API replica. The limits stop password guessing and email floods. Behind a reverse proxy, the proxy must set X-Forwarded-For, or all clients share each limit.
authentication.signInRateLimitHint: Per 10 seconds, including password and email changes.
authentication.emailRateLimitHint: Per minute, for password reset and email confirmation messages.
authentication.magicLinkRateLimitHint: Per minute, for requesting and opening sign-in links.
authentication.signInLimitInvalid: Enter a whole number from 1 to {max}.

storage.fileSizeHint: The largest single file an upload may carry. A bigger file is refused before it is stored.
storage.attachmentHint: Applies to issue attachments, files pasted into a description, and attachments added by agents.
storage.avatarHint: The profile picture people upload for their account.
storage.mimeTypesHint: One content type per line. Leave empty to accept any file.
storage.mimeTypesNote: A line is a full type (application/pdf) or a wildcard (image/*). Files already stored are kept whatever the list says.
storage.quotaHint: Total attachment storage one project may use. 0 means no limit.
storage.quotaNote: Once a project reaches the quota, new uploads are refused until someone deletes attachments.

jobs.range: Enter a whole number from {min, number} to {max, number}.
jobs.webhookLeaseNote: Set a lease longer than the timeout. Leases are in seconds, timeouts in milliseconds.
jobs.webhookTimeoutNote: Set a timeout shorter than the lease. Leases are in seconds, timeouts in milliseconds.
jobs.agentLeaseNote: Set a lease longer than the timeout under Agents with an endpoint URL. Leases are in seconds, timeouts in milliseconds.
jobs.invocationTimeoutNote: Set a timeout shorter than the leases under Agent runs and Agent chat. Leases are in seconds, timeouts in milliseconds.

webhooks.title: Webhooks
webhooks.description: How deliveries are sent and retried, when a failing webhook is turned off, and how long the log is kept.
webhooks.pollIntervalMsHint: How often queued deliveries and notifications are sent.
webhooks.batchSizeHint: How many deliveries are sent per check.
webhooks.timeoutMsHint: How long the receiving server has to answer before the attempt fails.
webhooks.maxAttemptsHint: How many times a delivery is sent before it is saved as failed.
webhooks.disableThresholdHint: The webhook is turned off after this many failed attempts in a row, retries included.
webhooks.leaseSecondsHint: An interrupted delivery is sent again after this time.
webhooks.retentionDaysHint: Successful deliveries are deleted from the log after this time. Failed ones stay.
webhooks.cleanupIntervalMinutesHint: How often old entries are deleted from the delivery log.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: Email and Telegram notifications. They are sent at the Check interval set under Webhooks.
notifications.batchSizeHint: How many notifications are sent per check.
notifications.maxAttemptsHint: How many times a notification is sent before it is saved as failed.
notifications.leaseSecondsHint: An interrupted notification is sent again after this time.

imports.title: Imports
imports.pollIntervalMsHint: How often queued imports are started.

agentRuns.title: Agent runs
agentRuns.description: How queued and scheduled agent runs start and retry.
agentRuns.pollIntervalMsHint: How often runs are taken from the queue and due schedules are queued.
agentRuns.maxAttemptsHint: How many times a run is started before it is saved as failed.
agentRuns.leaseSecondsHint: An interrupted run starts again after this time. For internal agents this time is never shorter than Run time limit in General.

agentChat.title: Agent chat
agentChat.description: Chats with external agents, through a runner or an endpoint URL.
agentChat.leaseSecondsHint: An interrupted answer starts again after this time.
agentChat.maxAttemptsHint: How many times the agent gets a message before the answer is saved as failed.
agentChat.claimWaitMsHint: How long a runner request waits for a new chat message.
agentChat.claimPollMsHint: A new chat message reaches a waiting runner within this time.
agentChat.streamPollMsHint: How often an open chat shows new parts of the answer.
agentChat.historyMessagesHint: How many earlier chat messages the agent gets with each new one.

agentInvocations.title: Agents with an endpoint URL
agentInvocations.description: Tasks and chat messages sent to an agent's endpoint URL.
agentInvocations.pollIntervalMsHint: How often queued tasks and chat messages are sent to these agents.
agentInvocations.timeoutMsHint: How long the endpoint has to answer. If it is late, the task or message is sent again when its lease ends.

sweeps.title: Archive and cleanup
sweeps.description: How often stale closed issues are archived, and old run traces and expired public links deleted.
sweeps.autoArchiveMinutesHint: How often stale closed issues are archived in projects with Archive turned on.
sweeps.tracePruneMinutesHint: How often run traces older than Keep run traces in General are deleted.
sweeps.shareExpiryMinutesHint: How often expired public links are deleted. A link stops opening when it expires, whatever this value is.

bot.title: Telegram bot
bot.description: How fast the bot picks up a change to its settings.
bot.configPollIntervalMsHint: A change under Telegram reaches the bot within this time.

telegram.botConfigured: People connect their Telegram account by opening a chat with this bot from their profile.
telegram.botMissing: Create a bot with @BotFather in Telegram and paste its token here.
telegram.botTokenHint: The token is verified with Telegram when you save, so a wrong one is refused here rather than failing silently later.
telegram.resolvedHint: Resolved from the token. This is the bot people will see when connecting.

email.providerHint: Choose one provider. Credentials are stored encrypted.
email.fromHint: Required for Resend. With SMTP it defaults to the username.
email.teamNotificationsHint: Let teams deliver their notifications through this provider instead of configuring one of their own. Each team still chooses whether to use it.
email.testHint: Send a real message with the current settings without saving them.
email.testConfigureFirst: Enable a provider and add its required credentials first.
email.microsoft365Hint: Signs in as an app registration in Entra ID instead of with the mailbox password, so the mailbox can keep MFA on. The app needs the Office 365 Exchange Online application permission SMTP.SendAsApp with admin consent, access to this mailbox in Exchange, and SMTP AUTH turned on for the mailbox.

emailTemplates.blankText: Add the missing subject or text to save
emailTemplates.subject: Subject
emailTemplates.removeUnknownVariables: Remove the unknown variables to save
emailTemplates.testNeedsProvider: Set up the email provider first
emailTemplates.requiredPlaceholders: Add {names} to the layout to save
emailTemplates.previewFailed: The preview didn't load. Reload the page to try again.

test.name: Test email
test.hint: Sent by the test button on the Email provider page.

authProvider.googleConfigured: An address without an account gets one; an address that already has a confirmed account signs into it.
authProvider.googleMissing: Add the client ID and secret first.
authProvider.redirectUriHint: Register this on the OAuth client in the Google Cloud console. Google refuses the sign-in if it does not match exactly.
authProvider.oidcConfigured: An address without an account gets one; an address that already has a confirmed account signs into it.
authProvider.oidcMissing: Add the discovery URL, client ID and secret first.
authProvider.discoveryUrlHint: Your provider's .well-known/openid-configuration. The authorization, token and userinfo endpoints are read from it.
authProvider.oidcLabelHint: Names your provider on the sign-in button. Leave it empty for a generic label.
authProvider.scopesHint: Separated by spaces. openid is required; profile and email fill in the name and address.
authProvider.oidcRedirectUriHint: Register this as a redirect URI on the client at your identity provider. The provider refuses the sign-in if it does not match exactly.
